text:
alex: quick check — about to apply a terraform change that currently adds a ClusterRoleBinding for the s3-uploader service account in namespace payments-staging so it can list buckets. is that overly broad? thinking Role + RoleBinding scoped to the namespace + IRSA instead. also want to avoid mounting static creds.

maria: prefer Role/RoleBinding unless you actually need cross-namespace permissions. clusterrolebinding is a blunt instrument. for S3 access you can scope the IAM policy to specific bucket prefixes and attach it to the IRSA role via the annotation: `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. :+1:

jonathan: agree with @maria. if you need to list buckets in the whole account that's one thing, but usually apps only need specific prefixes. example k8s manifests we use: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: s3-uploader
  namespace: payments-staging
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-s3-uploader-staging
---
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: s3-uploader-role
  namespace: payments-staging
rules:
- apiGroups: ['']
  resources: ['secrets']
  verbs: ['get']
---
kind: RoleBinding
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: s3-uploader-binding
  namespace: payments-staging
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: s3-uploader-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: s3-uploader
  namespace: payments-staging
```
this keeps k8s permissions local and IAM scoped via IRSA.

tara: one gotcha — double-check that the cluster OIDC provider is configured for the aws account you're deploying into. run `aws iam list-open-id-connect-providers` or look in the EKS cluster describe output. also avoid mounting AWS creds in secrets; IRSA + projected tokens is the right pattern.

alex: good points. my terraform change currently had a resource named `aws_eks_cluster_role_binding.s3_uploader` — i'll convert it to role + rolebinding. @ci-bot can you run a plan only for the eks.payments module?

ci-bot: ci-bot: running `terraform plan -target=module.eks.payments`... plan finished with warnings: 1) hardcoded account id detected in `aws_iam_role` resource; 2) plan would add `kubernetes_cluster_role_binding.s3-uploader-crb` (cluster-scoped) — flagged for review.

maria: if you push the TF change as a small focused PR i'll review. add a test that attempts to assume the role from a pod in another namespace (should fail).

jonathan: small nit: for token projection details, K8s bound service account token behavior -> IRSA relies on projected tokens + AWS STS. you don't need `automountServiceAccountToken: false` here; instead rely on the projected token semantics. if you want to tighten TTL, check the kubelet flags / bound token settings.

tara: also add a note in the PR about KMS key access if the policy allows PutObject with SSE-KMS. we had a hit once where policy allowed S3 but not the KMS key.

alex: thanks all — i'll open PR with Role/RoleBinding, update the TF to use a variable for account id, and set the annotation to `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-s3-uploader-staging`. PR link: https://github.com/redwoodinc/infra/pull/4217 — PTAL when ready. :pray:

ci-bot: ci-bot: PR 4217 — terraform plan succeeded for module.eks.payments in sandbox. cluster_role changes removed. warnings cleared (account id var added).
